questions.question_description: Write a C program to sort an array of integers using Insertion Sort. To prevent algorithm evasion, you MUST print the entire array state after placing each picked element into its sorted position.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the space-separated array on a new line after each insertion iteration. For N>=2, output N-1 lines. For N=0 output an empty line, and for N=1 output a single line with the element.
questions.hints: Maintain a sorted sub-array at the beginning. Take the next element, 'insert' it, and print the entire array.
questions.solution_explanation: Intermediate state printing prevents algorithm evasion.

questions.question_description: Write a C program to sort an array of integers using Selection Sort. To prevent algorithm evasion, you MUST print the entire array state after finding each minimum and swapping it.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the space-separated array on a new line after each outer loop pass. For N>=2, output N-1 lines. For N=0 output an empty line, and for N=1 output a single line with the element.
questions.hints: Find the minimum element in the unsorted portion, swap it with the first unsorted element, then print the array.
questions.solution_explanation: Intermediate state printing prevents algorithm evasion.

questions.question_description: Write a C program to sort an array of integers using Shell Sort. Use a standard gap sequence halving the distance each time (N/2, N/4, ... 1). Print the array after completing all shifts for a specific gap size.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the space-separated array on a new line after entirely processing each gap size. For N<=1, behave identically to standard edge case outputs.
questions.hints: Loop `for(int gap=n/2; gap>0; gap/=2)`, perform an insertion sort variant for that phase, and print the array.
questions.solution_explanation: Intermediate state printing enforces Shell Sort gaps.

questions.question_description: Write a C program to sort an array using the Merge Sort algorithm (Divide and Conquer approach). You MUST print the entire array state immediately after every sub-array merge operation finishes.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the full space-separated array on a new line after each successful `merge`.
questions.hints: Divide the array into halves, sort them recursively, and merge. Print the global array at the very end of your `merge` function.
questions.solution_explanation: Merge sort relies on printing after the merge step is completely finished, leaving an exact execution fingerprint.

questions.question_description: Write a C program to sort an array using Quick Sort with a pivot element. Pick the last element as your pivot. You MUST print the entire array state immediately after every successful partition operation.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the full space-separated array on a new line after each `partition`.
questions.hints: Pick a pivot (last element), partition the array, and IMMEDIATELY print the global array state before recursing into the lower and upper halves.
questions.solution_explanation: Printing after the partition routine locks the student into a strict subset of Quick Sort algorithm steps.

questions.question_description: Write a C program to sort an array of integers using Heap Sort by first building a heap and then extracting elements. You MUST print the initial fully built max heap array in one line, and then print the array state after EACH element extraction.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the max heap structure first. Then print the array after every max element is bubbled to the end.
questions.hints: Build a Max Heap and print it. Then repeatedly extract the maximum element (root), swap it with the last element of the remaining heap, re-heapify, and PRINT the array.
questions.solution_explanation: Printing after extraction shows the gradual assembly of the sorted subarray at the end of the heap.
